title: Document field
description: One entry in a document's fields[] array in data/documents.json. Replaces the old flat {id, label, placeholder, required} shape with enough structure to drive a schema-aware wizard (Phase 2.3) instead of one generic text-input renderer for every field regardless of what it actually asks for.

id.description: camelCase, unique within the document. Also the {{placeholder}} name substituted into clause bodies/gaps.

label.description: Short label shown above the input.

type.description: Drives both the input control Phase 2.3's renderer shows and any type-appropriate validation. 'select'/'multiselect'/'boolean'/'signature' aren't produced by the automated migration (tools/migrate_fields.py) — nothing in the current flat text-field corpus justifies inferring them — but are real, supported types for later hand-curation or Phase 2.4's clause-level conditionals.

placeholder.description: The input's placeholder-attribute hint, shown grayed-out before the user types. May legitimately be phrased as a format hint rather than a literal example ("e.g., Jane Doe") — that distinction is exactly why 'example' exists as a separate property. Unchanged by the Phase 2.1 migration.

example.description: A realistic, literal value for this field — safe to drop directly into a rendered document or a test fixture and have it read sensibly, unlike 'placeholder' which may be instructional copy. Derived from 'placeholder' by tools/migrate_fields.py using the same e.g.-prefix-stripping and instruction-phrase override logic tests/golden/golden.js already used and validated for fixture generation (see GOLDEN_REVIEW.md) — this migration is what makes that logic a first-class part of the data instead of test-only.

whyWeAsk.description: Plain-language explanation of why the document needs this field. Not populated by the Phase 2.1 migration — that's Phase 2.2b, deliberately a separate pass so every one gets real drafted text instead of a placeholder sentence.

helpText.description: Optional longer-form help shown on request (not populated by the Phase 2.1 migration).

default.description: Optional pre-filled value when the wizard first renders (not populated by the Phase 2.1 migration — no current field has an evident universal default).

pattern.description: A regex the value must match.

min.description: Numeric/date lower bound, for money/integer/percent/date types.

max.description: Numeric/date upper bound, for money/integer/percent/date types.

validation.description: Not populated by the Phase 2.1 migration. Left for hand-curation once Phase 2.3's renderer actually enforces these — writing constraints nothing checks yet would just be unverified guesses.

field.description: Another field's id in the same document.

showIf.description: Conditional visibility based on another field's answer. Nothing in the current schema has this yet — no document has conditional fields — so this is Phase 2.4's job, not the 2.1 migration's. Defined here now so validate_corpus.py's Phase 2.1 extension can check referenced ids exist and there are no cycles, ready for when real showIf values appear.

sensitive.description: True for data sensitive enough to exclude from analytics (Phase 8.1) or optionally skip syncing (Phase 7.4) — the migration marks this confidently only for unambiguous identifiers (SSN/ITIN, a trust's taxpayer ID); a fuller privacy-sensitivity audit of all 822 field ids is real future work, not something a migration script should guess at broadly.

sharedFieldId.description: Links to a canonical definition in schema/fields/ (Phase 2.2). Not populated by the Phase 2.1 migration — the shared library doesn't exist yet, this migration is what it gets built against next.
